name: Question 15
problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$ at the point where $t=\pi .$
worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(\pi ),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩=⟨2,0⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${r}^{″}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩=⟨0,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and ${r}^{″}(\pi )$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi ) & =⟨2,\,0,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-2\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=\pi $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi ){‖}^{3}}=\frac{2}{{2}^{3}}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of r(t)=⟨t−sin⁡t,1−cos⁡t⟩ at the point where t=π.

a
2
b
4
c
14
d
12
e
18
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The curvature κ(t) is given by

κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3.

First, we calculate r′(t), r′(π), and ‖r′(π)‖:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(t−sin⁡t),ddt(1−cos⁡t)⟩=⟨1−cos⁡t,sin⁡t⟩r′(π)=⟨1−cos⁡π,sin⁡π⟩=⟨2,0⟩‖r′(π)‖=22+02=2

Now, we find r″(t) and r″(π):

r″(t)=⟨ddt(1−cos⁡t),ddt(sin⁡t)⟩=⟨sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩r″(π)=⟨sin⁡π,cos⁡π⟩=⟨0,−1⟩

Next, we compute the cross product by considering r′(π) and r″(π) as 3-dimensional vectors with zero z-components:

r′(π)×r″(π)=⟨2,0,0⟩×⟨0,−1,0⟩=ijk2000−10=200−1k=−2k‖r′(π)×r″(π)‖=2

Therefore, the curvature at t=π is

κ(π)=‖r′(π)×r″(π)‖‖r′(π)‖3=223=14.
